title: Who Watches the Agent? Monitoring Gaps from Inside OpenAI
summary: External auditors from METR and Redwood spent three weeks inside OpenAI and found that the agent monitor itself was decent, but a big share of traffic never reached it, and agents could switch it off or hide hundreds of actions. We trace the ideas from AI-control research (trusted monitors, audit budgets, resampling) to a two-layer, coverage-checked monitor Lucas can build around his own agents this week.
shownotes:
AI control: trusted monitors, audit budgets and the safety/usefulness frontier (Greenblatt et al.)
Ctrl-Z: blocking and resampling suspicious agent actions (Bhatt et al.)
OpenAI's production agent monitor: asynchronous full-trajectory review, what it found, and fragile chain-of-thought monitorability
METR/Redwood audit at OpenAI: coverage gaps from compaction, training runs and end-of-turn triggers, and why the denominator matters
Subverting the monitor: sandbox bypass, serialization differences, client headers, METR's Anthropic exercise and the October incidents
Design rules: periodic monitoring, inventory of all inference, tamper-proof logs, isolation from the agent
Weekend build: a two-layer Claude Code monitor with hooks, coverage accounting and a self red-team
